s: vinyl, single-origin coffee and quirky décor in a Chueca corner
w: A small Chueca café-slash-concept-store where bicycles on the walls and skull graffiti sit alongside racks of vinyl and vintage objects, jazz playing over careful single-origin coffee. Playful rather than precious, and a genuine local hangout a block off Chueca's busier drag.
_facts: Located at Calle de San Lucas 9, 28004 Madrid, Chueca
Combines a specialty coffee bar with a vinyl records and vintage-object concept store
Known for eclectic, quirky interior decor

s: a communal, living-room-style café at the heart of Malasaña
w: A relaxed, sociable café on Corredera Baja de San Pablo, in the middle of Malasaña, built around simple good things -- solid coffee, avocado toast, easy plates -- and a living-room feel that keeps neighbours and creatives lingering rather than just passing through.
_facts: Located at Corredera Baja de San Pablo 51, 28004 Madrid, Malasaña
Known for a cosy, communal atmosphere and simple, well-made food (avocado toast, brunch plates)
A long-standing specialty coffee anchor of the Malasaña neighbourhood

s: the market that captures Lavapiés's messy, multicultural, creative energy
w: A municipal market that has grown well past groceries into the fullest expression of Lavapiés itself -- traditional Spanish stalls beside international food counters, secondhand books sold by weight, a Japanese multi-use space, handmade jewellery stands and community events. Chaotic in the best sense, and entirely local rather than curated for visitors.
_facts: Located at Calle Embajadores 41, 28012 Madrid, Lavapiés
Municipal market building with additional entrances on Calle del Sombrerete and Calle de Tribulete
Mixes traditional grocery stalls with international food vendors, a secondhand bookshop and cultural/event spaces
Reachable via Embajadores or Lavapiés metro stations (Line 3)

s: a gritty, global crossroads market with a flamenco school upstairs
w: A loud, unpolished market on the border of Lavapiés and Centro where traditional butchers and fishmongers trade beside sushi, tacos, arepas and ramen counters, while the rhythms of a flamenco school upstairs filter down through the stalls. Everyday Madrid rather than a curated food-hall experience.
_facts: Located at Calle de Santa Isabel 5, 28012 Madrid, on the Lavapiés/Centro border
Traditional municipal market mixing Spanish butchers/fishmongers with international food stalls
Houses a flamenco academy on an upper floor
